Why do gas markets matter for power market planning?
US power and gas markets are becoming increasingly interconnected. After years of relatively flat electricity demand, data centres and other large loads are accelerating power demand, while LNG exports and changing regional gas flows are creating additional competition for gas supply.
For utilities, developers and other power-market participants, understanding the power outlook increasingly means looking beyond the electricity market itself. Fuel availability, pipeline infrastructure, LNG demand and regional gas dynamics can all influence where gas-fired generation is viable and how its economics develop. 
Our new infographic explores five gas-market developments reshaping US power markets, including:

Why growing power demand is becoming a bigger driver of gas demand
How LNG exports could create greater competition for gas supply
Why pipeline development matters for where gas can move
How regional gas dynamics can affect generation and load growth
Why oil markets and geopolitics can still influence the power-market picture
